newsitem.title: USA: IMF says Yeltsin illness will not hamper loans.
newsitem.headline: IMF says Yeltsin illness will not hamper loans.

text.p: International Monetary Fund Managing Director Michel Camdessus on Thursday said its vast loan programme to Russia was not being hampered by the serious health problems of Russian President Boris Yeltsin.

"It (Yeltsin's health) does not affect at all our disbursements," he said in an interview with Reuters Financial Television, adding: "I don't perceive any vacuum in the way our programme with Russia is being implemented..."
The IMF has been disbursing its $10 billion loan programme on a monthly basis, closely monitoring whether the authorities are keeping the economy on track, and will continue to do so.
"We have continued disbursing month after month...and we intend to continue," he said.
Camdessus described Yeltsin as the "key man" in Russia and said it was important for the country to have a president in good health.
But he said the IMF programme with Russia did not require presidential measures. "What is needed is central bank and government ready to continue to implement their pledges and they are doing that."
The Camdesuss remarks come as the extent of Yeltsin's illness and its effect on Russia are increasingly being known.
Doctors Wednesday said Yeltsin was fit enough to have heart surgery but they delayed his planned bypass operation for at least six weeks to improve the chances of success.
Chief Kremlin physician Sergei Mironov told NTV commercial television that Yeltsin was working two to three hours a day.

The post-operation recovery period might be about two months, but Mironov said Yeltsin could start work sooner. Asked when he could take back the "nuclear button" which controls Russia's strategic weapons, he said:
"I think after 24 hours, after he has completely come around from the anaesthetic."

Yeltsin will hand over supreme power to Chernomyrdin, his constitutional stand-in, shortly before the operation. The premier has already assumed some of Yeltsin's responsibilities for coordinating the work of the Defence and Security Ministries.

Meanwhile, security chief Alexander Lebed, painting a picture of deep instability in Russia as Yeltsin prepares for surgery, said on Thursday that Russia was on the brink of chaos and the army could soon mutiny.
